newsitem.title: UK: IBCA ups Uruguay long-term foreign currency rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA ups Uruguay long-term foreign currency rating.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it had upgraded the Oriental Republic of Uruguay's long-term foreign currency rating to an investment grade rating of BBB minus from BB plus.
At the same time IBCA upgraded Uruguay's short term foreign currency rating, which applies to debt maturing in less than one year, to A3 from B.
"The upgrade from BB plus makes Uruguay only the third Latin American country to have an investment grade rating," IBCA said in a statement.
"The rating will apply to all senior, unsecured sovereign debt issues and to Uruguay's Brady bonds, and serve as a ceiling for IBCA credit ratings of banks and corporates in Uruguay."
IBCA cited the significant progress made in fiscal consolidation, which had underpinned the stabilisation programme and led to steady reductions in inflation, as reasons for the upgrade.

"In addition the pension reform removes a worry about the long-term sustainability of fiscal adjustment, and will underpin growth of national savings and investment, and help the economy become less reliant on foreign capital inflows," the rating agency said.

"Although Uruguay is exposed to developments in its two large neighbours - Argentina and Brazil - and the Uruguayan recovery would be vulnerable to a serious reversal in either country, this would be unlikely to impede debt service," IBCA said.

"Moreover, the post-Mexico crisis showed that Uruguay's position as a regional banking centre and recipient of capital flight puts it in an advantageous position even during a severe regional stress test."
IBCA said the speed of structural reform was likely to accelerate because of changes in the political system.

"Results of the December 1996 referendum herald changes to the electoral law which should discourage the factionalism that hitherto has characterised Uruguayan political life, and should lead to more cohesive parties, governments and policy-making," the agency said.

"The constraints on the rating remain worries about the extent of adjustment to the liberalisation entailed by Mercousur, the sedate pace of reform and the stability of the net external debt ratios given the modest pace of export and GDP growth," IBCA said.
